pick.headline: Iran's Prime Minister Bazargan resigns
pick.summary: On November 6, 1979, two days after the seizure of the US Embassy, Mehdi Bazargan resigned as prime minister of Iran's provisional government.
pick.significance: Bazargan's fall removed the last moderate leadership willing to deal with Washington and left power with Khomeini's Revolutionary Council, prolonging the hostage crisis.
pick.fbis: The November 6, 1979, Middle East & North Africa report listed Iranian items on Khomeyni accepting Bazargan's resignation and delegating power, with the text of the letter of resignation.

alternates.headline: M-19 guerrillas seize Colombia's Palace of Justice
alternates.summary: On November 6, 1985, guerrillas of the M-19 movement stormed the Palace of Justice in Bogota and took the Supreme Court justices hostage. The army's assault over the next day left about a hundred dead, including eleven justices.
alternates.significance: The siege and its violent end were among the darkest episodes of Colombia's conflicts, and fed suspicion of links between the guerrillas and the drug cartels then fighting extradition to the United States.
alternates.fbis: The Latin America report of November 7, 1985, led its Colombia section with M-19 rebels occupying the Palace of Justice and taking hostages, including an M-19 communique and a spokesman saying the war begins now.
